title: WHAT WE KNOW
sub: Two sisters led a revolt against the Han Empire. The earliest surviving written accounts we have are Chinese. The main Vietnamese chronicle came many centuries later.
say: Two sisters led a revolt against the Han Empire. The earliest surviving written accounts we have are Chinese. The main Vietnamese chronicle came many centuries later.

title: 40 CE
sub: Around the year 40, Jiaozhi was a commandery of the Han Empire, governed by Su Ding.
say: Around the year forty, Jyao-jir was a commandery of the Han Empire, governed by Soo Ding.

title: THE REVOLT
sub: Trưng Trắc, from a leading local family, rose up with her sister Trưng Nhị. The Han history says they took sixty-five towns, and that Trưng Trắc made herself queen.
say: Chung Chack, from a leading local family, rose up with her sister Chung Nyee. The Han history says they took sixty-five towns, and that Chung Chack made herself queen.

title: WHY?
sub: Why did she revolt? The Vietnamese chronicle says Su Ding restrained her by law and killed her husband, Thi Sách. The Han account says he restrained Trưng Trắc herself by law, and she rebelled in anger.
say: Why did she revolt? The Vietnamese chronicle says Soo Ding restrained her by law and killed her husband, Tee Sack. The Han account says he restrained Chung Chack herself by law, and she rebelled in anger.

title: MA YUAN
sub: In 41 or 42, Han records say General Ma Yuan was sent against the revolt. By 43, it had been suppressed.
say: In forty-one or forty-two, Han records say General Mah Yoo-en was sent against the revolt. By forty-three, it had been suppressed.

title: HOW DID THEY DIE?
sub: Chinese records say the sisters were beheaded. The main Vietnamese chronicle says they died in battle. Later traditions say they took their own lives.
say: Chinese records say the sisters were beheaded. The main Vietnamese chronicle says they died in battle. Later traditions say they took their own lives.

sub: The main Vietnamese chronicle, the Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư, was completed in 1479, more than fourteen centuries after the revolt.
say: The main Vietnamese chronicle, the Dye Vee-et Suh Kee Twan Too, was completed in fourteen seventy-nine, more than fourteen centuries after the revolt.

title: LEGEND
sub: In later Vietnamese memory, the sisters became revered figures. Temples and public places commemorate them today.
say: In later Vietnamese memory, the sisters became revered figures. Temples and public places commemorate them today.

title: TWO VIEWS
sub: Han records describe a rebellion in Jiaozhi. Later Vietnamese accounts remember the sisters as figures of resistance to Han rule.
say: Han records describe a rebellion in Jyao-jir. Later Vietnamese accounts remember the sisters as figures of resistance to Han rule.

title: RICE & EMPIRES
sub: What we know is small. What it came to mean is huge. Follow for more.
